S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

info.persona: Lawson Royal is a 62‑year‑old sustainable farmer‑artist whose boundless curiosity fuels watercolor skies and blues riffs, yet their propensity to worry and occasional disorganization keeps them juggling grant proposals, garden chores, and midnight poetry drafts.
info.professional_persona: Lawson Royal, a seasoned sustainable farmer with expertise in crop rotation, livestock care, and farm machinery maintenance, leverages their vivid imagination and improvisational problem‑solving to mentor younger workers, incorporate water‑conservation practices, and envision an agro‑art retreat where teaching gardening meets watercolor painting and community storytelling.
info.cultural_background: Lawson is a Black South Carolinian whose family roots trace back generations in Lancaster County, a region shaped by agrarian labor and close‑knit community ties. He grew up within a church-centered environment where music, oral storytelling, and mutual aid were daily practices. This heritage instilled in him a deep respect for collective well‑being, intergenerational knowledge sharing, and the resilience cultivated during the Civil Rights era and the legacy of sharecropping. These cultural influences permeate his artistic expression, his commitment to sustainable agriculture, and his dedication to mentoring younger members of his community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Lawson immerses himself in watercolor painting of the Lowcountry sky, plays blues guitar at local gatherings, and writes poetry that reflects his inner curiosity about abstract concepts. He is an avid reader of speculative fiction, tends to an heirloom vegetable garden, and enjoys birdwatching along the nearby Swamp Creek. Community events such as craft fairs and storytelling evenings energize him, and he often prepares traditional soul‑food meals for family celebrations. To manage his tendency toward worry, he practices mindfulness meditation and explores genealogy to connect with his ancestors.
info.sports_persona: Lawson Royal enjoys low‑impact fitness through weekly pickleball matches with the Lowcountry Senior Club, follows the Charleston Battery soccer team and the South Carolina Gamecocks football program, and participates in seasonal bird‑watching hikes that double as cardio walks along Swamp Creek.
info.arts_persona: Lawson Royal channels their love of blues guitar into impromptu jam sessions inspired by B.B. King and Muddy Waters, creates atmospheric watercolor skies reminiscent of John Singer Sargent, carves wooden talismans while listening to contemporary folk artist Rhiannon Giddens, and draws narrative inspiration from poet Mary Oliver.
info.travel_persona: Lawson Royal favors purposeful travel, having explored the historic streets of Charleston, the riverfront of Savannah, and the mountain art community of Asheville, while dreaming of a watercolor pilgrimage to the cliffs of Cinque Terre and the lavender fields of Provence, always planning trips around modest budgets and family commitments.
info.culinary_persona: Lawson Royal, an adept home cook, prepares soulful meals like shrimp and grits, smoked collard greens, and sweet potato pie using garden‑fresh okra, heirloom tomatoes, smoked paprika, and fresh thyme, while occasionally indulging in a pit‑smoked brisket at family gatherings and meticulously sourcing local honey for glaze.

info.persona: Shamis Walker, a puzzle‑loving, methodical 20‑year‑old, balances a competitive drive for retail success with quiet yoga sessions, spontaneous watercolor journaling, and a healthy skepticism that keeps both cash drawers and personal ambitions meticulously in check.
info.professional_persona: Shamis Walker, a 20‑year‑old retail associate, leverages their meticulous cash‑handling expertise, data‑driven sales tracking, and emerging digital‑payment knowledge to mentor peers while competitively pursuing rapid promotion to assistant manager.
info.cultural_background: Shamis grew up in the suburban town of Chatham in Morris County, New Jersey, within a middle-class, white American family likely tracing its roots to European ancestry. The region’s East-Coast suburban culture emphasizes education, punctuality, a strong work ethic, and community involvement through events such as town fairs, high-school sports, and seasonal activities like apple picking. While her immediate environment is relatively homogeneous, the broader New Jersey setting exposed her to a diverse population, fostering a respectful but cautious attitude toward different perspectives. These cultural influences have reinforced her organized, reliable nature and her balanced outlook on new ideas and traditional methods.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her free time, Shamis enjoys reading mystery and thriller novels, solving Sudoku and crossword puzzles, and listening to business and technology podcasts, which satisfy her curiosity. She regularly hikes the trails of nearby parks such as Latta Pond and enjoys practicing yoga to balance her social energy with alone time. Shamis also sketches in a watercolor journal, plays acoustic guitar at small gatherings, volunteers at the local food pantry, and experiments with photography, capturing the changing seasons of her New Jersey hometown.
info.sports_persona: Shamis Walker spends weekends tackling the trails of Latta Pond with the Middlesex County Hiking Club, rounds out fitness through nightly yoga sessions, and cheers for the New York Knicks, New Jersey Devils, and New York Giants while occasionally joining a community pick‑up soccer game during summer.
info.arts_persona: Shamis Walker channels their curiosity into watercolor sketches of New Jersey’s changing seasons, strums acoustic renditions of John Mayer and Fleet Foxes at neighborhood gatherings, and captures candid moments inspired by Annie Leibovitz’s portrait style, while finding literary thrills in Agatha Christie novels.
info.travel_persona: Shamis Walker prefers meticulously planned weekend getaways—like a budget‑friendly road trip to Shenandoah National Park and a day‑long subway stroll through Manhattan’s museum district—while dreaming of future solo hikes in Yosemite and a cultural immersion trip to Edinburgh, Scotland.
info.culinary_persona: Shamis Walker, an amateur home cook, gravitates toward wholesome dishes such as quinoa‑seed bowls with roasted cherry tomatoes, basil pesto pasta, and avocado toast topped with chili flakes, while savoring the occasional New Jersey‑style pizza slice and experimenting with seasonal pumpkin soup during autumn.

info.persona: Danny Neal is a compassionate, energetic science educator who balances meticulous planning with spontaneous creativity, they channel calm resilience into every pursuit, and they occasionally over‑indulge in gadget‑shopping and late‑night kitchen experiments.
info.professional_persona: Danny Neal, a 32‑year‑old secondary‑school science teacher in Atlanta, merges inquiry‑based labs, Google Classroom, and data‑driven feedback to create engaging lessons while they channel their sociable, compassionate nature into mentorship, conflict mediation, and collaborative curriculum innovation.
info.cultural_background: Danny was raised in a middle‑class, Anglo‑American family in the suburban outskirts of Atlanta. He identifies with Southern cultural values such as hospitality, community involvement, and a strong work ethic. Growing up, he attended a local Baptist church, which reinforced his sense of service and compassion. His family’s heritage includes roots in the Appalachian region, and he maintains traditions like Sunday family meals featuring fried chicken, collard greens, and sweet tea. Living in DeKalb County, he embraces the neighborhood’s cultural diversity, regularly engaging in multicultural festivals and supporting local artists, which enrich his inclusive worldview.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Danny thrives on social and active pursuits. He regularly plays pickup basketball at a local community center, participates in weekend cycling groups that explore Atlanta’s BeltLine and nearby trails, and volunteers as a youth mentor at a neighborhood after‑school program. His curiosity leads him to tinker with DIY electronics kits and experiment with cooking Southern comfort foods with a modern twist. He also enjoys attending live music events in Decatur, reading science popular‑culture books, and practicing mindfulness meditation to maintain his calm and resilient demeanor.
info.sports_persona: Danny Neal regularly joins Saturday evening pickup basketball at the West End Community Center, rides with the Atlanta BeltLine Cycling Club on weekend rides, cheers for the Atlanta Hawks, Falcons, and United, and they also coach a youth basketball squad at the neighborhood after‑school program.
info.arts_persona: Danny Neal attends live shows at Decatur’s 7 Stills Club, where they enjoy performances by The Avett Brothers and Tame Impala, reads popular‑science books by Carl Sagan and Neil deGrasse Tyson for inspiration, and they find creative release in tinkering with electronics the way they appreciate the experimental art of Brian Eno.
info.travel_persona: Danny Neal favors short, purposeful trips that blend culture and adventure, having road‑tripped to Asheville, explored Savannah’s historic streets, and spent a weekend music‑filled stay in New Orleans, while they keep a bucket‑list entry for hiking Iceland’s volcanic landscapes and sampling street food in Tokyo.
info.culinary_persona: Danny Neal enjoys cooking Southern comfort foods with a modern twist, often preparing fried chicken with kimchi slaw, collard greens sautéed with quinoa and smoked paprika, and skillet biscuits topped with truffle butter, using ingredients like buttermilk, hot sauce, and fresh herbs, while they experiment between enthusiastic home cooking and budding food‑tech tinkering.
